content.thinking:
I'm planning the scene layout in one pass: a workbench with a tabletop around 1.6m wide, and thinking through how the builder's joint and parenting requirements apply to plain prop objects versus parts needing a root joint.

I'll set up a single root joint for all parts to attach to, and sketch a helper for creating boxes with paint applied—using cel-shaded colors for most surfaces and flat shading for anything glowing, keeping within the flat-color limit since painted textures don't count against it. For wood textures, I'm layering a grain pattern wrapped in cel shading so it reads naturally lit and shadowed.

Now I'm laying out the actual geometry: the tabletop dimensions and height, a trim edge along the border, and four square legs positioned at the corners.

Adding shelf and apron details...

Now planning tabletop items: a stack of colorful books with gold trim and one open book on a stand, a balance scale with chains and pans holding small weights, and an assortment of potion flasks (round-bottom, vial, conical, heart-shaped) with glowing liquids, corks, labels, and star stoppers, keeping the glass simple without transparency.

I'm also adding a mortar and pestle with herbs, hanging herb bundles with leaf-card textures tied above on a rack beam, a potted plant with glowing blossoms, and a candle plus a distillation setup with a flask, burner, and coiled tube.

I'm planning a scroll, quill and ink pot, plus a glowing crystal on a gold cradle rather than floating freely. For the floor, I'm adding a rug with a painted pattern and maybe baskets of herbs or a barrel nearby.

Now I'm setting up helper functions to keep the code compact, around 400 lines, defining a builder root joint and shorthand functions for boxes and cylinders with shared bone and position options.

Writing cylinder/sphere helpers...

For bottles I'm thinking the profile should start with the neck radius rather than zero to avoid self-crossing, and since glow() rejects paint materials, I'll use flat glowing colors for liquid and keep the glass shell as a separate pale region near the neck rather than overlapping geometry.

Adding a highlight strip...

Now I'm sketching out a bottle spec schema with profile points for different shapes, like a round flask defined by a lathe profile with body curves and a flaring neck. Each bottle will be a glowing lathed shape clipped to the liquid level, layered under a separate glass shell.

I'm working out how glass and liquid should interface at the liquid boundary: the liquid lathes from the base up to the liquid height using interpolated radius, while the glass lathes only the upper portion so they don't overlap and flicker. I'll also need a radius-interpolation helper, a general bottle-building function taking profile, liquid height, position, and material params, plus separate pieces for corks, stoppers, and a gold neck ring.

Now I'm picking a Genshin-inspired color palette (warm wood, cream, gold, teal, purple, rose, green, navy) and planning SVG filigree textures for gold trim, sizing stroke widths so they stay crisp when rasterized at 512px.

I'm also designing a reusable label texture function with a cream rounded-rect background and a swirl/leaf symbol, plus a book-page texture with faint ruled lines, mapping the page texture onto a flat plane oriented so its top edge faces upward and back.

For the leaf cards, I'm sketching green leaf shapes with veins, plus variants like a lavender spike and a glowing flower, all tinted white for flexibility. For the rug, I'm painting it procedurally using position coordinates to create border bands and a diamond lattice pattern, centering it in the room at a modest size, and considering whether to add a rune detail to the crystal.

I'm also planning a scroll with map-like line texture lying on the table, and thinking through the back wall design—maybe a wood-plank panel with an alchemy circle decal, positioned to fit between or above the shelves, settling on rough dimensions for the backboard's width, height, and placement.

Now I'm working out shelf placement: boards at a couple heights with brackets, leaving a central area for the alchemy circle decal, flanked by shelves on either side sized to hold bottles without crowding, plus a hanging herb beam across the top supported by posts rising from the backboard.

Adjusting the beam so it's mounted via brackets, with herb bundles hanging down just slightly overlapping the circle decal, and fine-tuning the depth positions of the beam, bundles, and decal relative to the wall surface so nothing clips through the backboard.

I'm also adding a small glowing lantern hanging near the beam's end for visual interest, and defining a reusable bundle function that generates a cluster of leaning card frames to represent tied herb stems, with slight rotation variation across each card for a natural look.

I need to account for the fact that cards drawn facing the downstream flow direction appear upside down from this viewing angle (root edge at top), so I'm adjusting the card geometry so the root stays attached at the top while the visible drawing orientation compensates for that flip.

I'm adding a potted plant with glowing flower cards and varied leaning angles, a woven basket for herbs, and a stack of books built from cover boxes with inset page blocks and visible spines.

Still writing book geometry...

Still writing helper functions...

Now thinking through the book stack on the table with varying sizes and tilt angles, plus upright shelf books with gold spine bands and title details facing forward.

For the balance scale on the right, I'm planning out the lathe-turned base and pillar, the gold beam with hanging pans, chains made of thin rods, and brass weights, with one pan holding a glowing gem and the beam tilted slightly for asymmetry.

Building the beam shape with decorative spherical tips, then attaching chains as thin rods connecting beam ends to pan rims at three angled points, and starting the lathe profile for the pan's bowl shape.

I'll add a helper function to auto-close bottle/pot profiles by mirroring the top and bottom back to the axis, keeping bowls explicit instead. For the lathe segments I'll use 10 for bottles with hard creases above 35°, then place a mortar and pestle near the front center—shaping the mortar as a stone bowl profile and starting the pestle with a rounded cap.

Now I'm sketching the pestle as a tilted capsule rod, scattering a few flattened green spheres inside the mortar to suggest herbs, and giving the mortar a cream-teal glaze with a gold rim band using a paint function that highlights the upper portion. Then I'm positioning an alembic/distillation setup to the back-left with a small burner, glowing flame, tripod stand, and a round flask on top.

Writing flask profile curve...

Skipping the coil wrap for simplicity, maybe adding a few ring bands along the path instead. Now I'm working out the overall layout plan, placing the scale, alembic, mortar, and bottle cluster across the tabletop within its bounds, starting with a books stack near the left edge.

Continuing the layout: I'm placing an open book on a lectern toward the front-left, positioning the alembic and its tube/receiver nearby, and adding a stack of books with a rolled scroll resting beside them, all mapped out with approximate coordinates and dimensions so nothing overlaps on the table.

Placing the alembic receiver and crystal, then scattering clutter near the open book—ink pot, quill, and a candlestick with glowing flame. Adding a potted plant on the table, positioning it carefully so its leaves don't collide with the scale's pans.

Now I'm laying out the shelves: left shelf holding jars and books/bottles at different heights, right shelf mirroring it. On the floor I'm adding a rug, a basket of herbs, a simple stool, and a crate beneath the shelf holding jars, pots, and a small bubbling cauldron with a glowing green liquid and gold handle.

Overall bounds come out to roughly 2.2 x 1.4 x 1.8, with everything resting properly on the floor plane (rug bottom at zero, legs centered appropriately) so sinking stays minimal. Now I'm moving into writing the actual scene code, double-checking which imports I'll need from the builder utilities so nothing ends up unused.

Writing imports and helper setup...

I'm defining wood grain colors for the table, varying the grain axis depending on whether it's a tabletop surface (horizontal grain) or legs (vertical grain), and working out texel density so the texture resolution matches the physical scale of the piece.

Now I'm bumping the paint sheet to 2048 for better resolution and deciding which materials get full painted textures (wood, rugs, book covers, pots) versus simple flat colors for small accent details like gold or brass, keeping the flat palette limited to around 30 colors to save atlas space.

Setting up the build structure now...

Defining helper functions and SVG filigree texture...

I'm matching the decal's 10:1 aspect ratio to the apron plane dimensions, placing it at the front face just outside the apron surface, and planning matching decals for the side aprons too.

Now I'm working out the full table geometry: tabletop dimensions and position, leg placement and sizing, and the front/back/side apron box dimensions aligned so the decal textures sit flush against their outer faces.

I'm also adding the finer details—a lower cross-shelf, gold foot caps and collars at the leg tops, a thin inlay band, and a gold trim strip along the top edge—placing each piece with precise coordinates so they read as decorative accents.

For the tabletop itself, I'm layering a thin inlaid cloth runner just above the wood surface, with a teal center and gold border painted via a simple condition on position, making sure items placed on top sit slightly above the runner's thickness.

Now I'm working out the rug paint function, using a radial/band distance metric to layer border, rose, gold, navy diamond pattern, and a teal medallion center, with dimensions sized to fit around the basket. Then I'm moving on to defining the books.

Each book has flat and upright variants, with an optional gold emblem texture (a star-and-circle SVG) placed on the top cover as a small plane oriented to face upward relative to the book's rotation. I'm also planning spine bands as thin boxes across the spine, and considering a simplified open book resting on a lectern or table.

I'm adding texture planes atop the page surfaces, then layering in details like a curled page edge, a hanging red ribbon bookmark from the gutter, and maybe a small glowing floating sigil above the book for extra atmosphere.

Now I'm designing a floating dendro-green glowing orb with thin gold rings above the open book, plus page texture details—faint handwritten lines, a small leaf illustration on the left page, and a cream background to keep the two page textures visually distinct.

For the potion bottles, I'm building a helper function that constructs each bottle as a lathed solid: the liquid body uses the profile points below the fill line with a glowing flat color, while the glass shell above it uses a separate lathe with a cool translucent tint to distinguish glass from liquid.

I'm adding finishing details too -- a thin gold ring at the neck, a cork plug cylinder seated into the opening, and a small stretched highlight sphere for shine. I'm positioning each bottle via a base coordinate and rel y-offset, then starting to define the actual profile point arrays (like a flask shape) that these lathe functions will consume.

Now I'm sketching coordinate profiles for several other glassware types -- a tall vial with its own liquid-level mark, a conical Erlenmeyer flask with its wider base tapering to a narrow neck, and I'm starting on a round pot-bellied shape too.

Working out the highlight sphere position so it sits exactly on the bottle's surface at that height, computing the radial direction and scaling the ellipsoid so it pokes out slightly from the faceted lathe surface.

Now I'm thinking through label plane placement — a small rounded label texture positioned flush against the tangent surface of the flask at the correct height and depth offset.

For narrower containers like the vial, I decide labels won't fit well, so I'll skip the texture there and use a simple string tag instead, while reserving conical shapes without labels too.

For reusing geometry across shelf containers, I'm structuring a reusable bottle-building function that takes a kind, position, liquid, and a scale factor so I can generate flasks, vials, cones, squat and square bottles all from one parameterized profile, organized into a kinds lookup table.

For jars, I'm defining a lathe profile with a slight neck taper and a lid, letting contents vary between glowing liquid or dried herb mounds made of small green cel-shaded spheres, reusing the bottle function with a wood-colored lid swap. I'm also sketching a bundle function for herb bundles with position and texture parameters.

Now I'm arranging card frames in a circular pattern around a center point, each angled outward, then feeding those frames into the card-rendering call with size, lean, flow direction, randomness, and spin settings so the herbs fan out naturally -- I'm considering making the flow direction vary per card index so the fanning looks less uniform.

Adding twine details and a suspension string from the beam down to the bundle, then starting on the leaf SVG texture with a curved outline path.

Still writing leaf and lavender textures...

For the remaining plant textures I'm adding mint with small teal-green circles along a stem and berry strands with red circles, then designing a glow-flower helper that builds a center ball plus six radial petal spheres for the pink/teal bloom effect.

Now moving to the potted plant, I'm shaping a lathe profile for a teal ceramic pot with a gold band.

For the basket's rim, I'm adding a closed ring sweep for the lip and an arc sweep for the handle, curving up from one side to the other. I'm painting the basket with a horizontal stripe pattern to mimic woven bands, then filling the inside with lavender and leaf foliage cards, using around 14 frames each for fullness.

I'm also placing a small wooden stool near the table with a cylindrical seat and three splayed legs, adding a cushion on top, and positioning a dark iron cauldron on the lower shelf with a rounded, bulging profile shape typical of a witch's pot.

Now I'm detailing the cauldron further: adding glowing green liquid inside, a slightly raised gold-iron rim, tube-arc handles, small conical legs, and a few tiny floating glowing bubbles above the rim for a magical bubbling effect. On the lower shelf I'm also adding a stack of flat books, a couple of jars, and a bundle of three horizontal scrolls for extra clutter detail.

I'm working out a scroll helper function that orients a paper cylinder along a given direction with wooden knob caps at each end and a ribbon band wrapped around the middle, then planning a hanging lantern near the top right of the shelf.

Checking the vertical layout, I realize that the lantern at x=0.72 would overlap with the bottles on the right shelf, so I need to reposition it toward the center, around x=0, aligning it with the beam bundle instead.

Extending the beam beyond the backboard width to ±0.95 so lanterns can hang at x=±0.93 without colliding with the shelf, checking clearance against shelf radius. I'm reconsidering how to support the beam since the backboard only reaches ±0.85 — rather than posts, I'll try wall-mounted brackets extending outward to the beam ends.

Widening the backboard to ±1.0 as a floating wall panel from y=0.87 to 1.78, with two square posts at x=±0.97 running floor to ceiling with gold caps, framing the board between them and a front beam attached near z=-0.30 for the hanging lanterns.

Checking the beam placement against post corners, it fits snugly against the edge. Now I'm working out lantern positions hanging at x=±0.88 near the posts, cross-checking against the shelf board span and making sure the lanterns don't collide with the shelf's depth or sit awkwardly relative to the board's top surface.

For the backboard, I'm sizing it between the posts at 1.86 wide and setting its vertical extent and thickness, then centering it. For the wall paint, I want vertical plank lines in a cool navy-teal tone to contrast the warm table, with subtle mottling for texture.

Writing wall paint shader...

I'm checking that the cel shading will read as lit given the wall's normal faces directly toward the light, which gives a comfortably visible brightness value. Now I'm moving on to designing an alchemy circle decal for the wall.

Writing SVG circle code...

I'm also planning gold trim strips for the wall, shelf brackets made from rotated boxes to suggest triangular supports, and considering whether small star decals or a hanging signboard are worth adding, though I'm leaning toward skipping the joint details to keep things simple.

I'll adjust tassel placement to x=±0.62, z=-0.30, hanging from the beam at y1.70 down through a ball, bell cone, and fringe tips ending around y1.60, keeping them clear of the shelf items at z=-0.22. Then I'll double-check that upper shelf items stay at or below 0.15 height to avoid any collision.

Now I'm adding more Genshin-inspired props: a floating glowing elemental sigil crystal, a candle setup with a lathe brass holder, cream cylinder candle, and an orange cone flame with inner glow and small drip spheres, plus an inkpot and quill piece with a leaf-shaped feather built from an extruded outline.

Working out feather orientation geometry...

Working out the quill's orientation lying flat with the nib pointing forward and feather trailing behind, computing rotation vectors to tilt it at roughly -25° for a natural resting angle.

Checking that the extrude options accept the direction vectors correctly, then moving to the feather's cream/teal coloring with a gold quill shaft, and starting the crystal cradle design with gold prong rods and a small octahedron gem.

For the tiny sparkle stars I'll scale octahedrons into thin diamond shapes and scatter about ten around the potions for a magical effect, keeping track of each part separately. I'm also laying out the full color palette now—golds, brasses, inks, corks, ribbon reds, and the various potion liquid hues like purple, teal, rose, amber, green, and blue, plus glass and flame tones.

Now I'm writing a helper function that interpolates radius along a bottle's profile curve by height, then building a bottle-construction function that takes a kind, position, liquid type, scale, and optional label texture to assemble the geometry.

Writing bottle construction code...

I realize there's an issue where the upper glass section closes off at the axis at the liquid line, which would create an unwanted solid disk there instead of an open rim.

Adding the cork ring on top, a small white highlight sphere on the liquid surface for a glassy sheen, and an optional label plane positioned against the bottle's curved radius.

I'm now building a label texture generator that creates small SVG icon badges (star, leaf, droplet shapes) in a rounded card with colored symbols, to decorate certain potion bottles.

Adding ground lines at the base, then working out bottle placement on the table by checking each item's radius against the table edge so nothing clips outside the 0.85 boundary—adjusting x-positions for the flask, squat bottle, and others to keep them within bounds.

I need to avoid collisions with the swinging pans overhead, which pass above anything under 0.125 height in that x-range. I'm repositioning the plant and the amber cone out of the pan's path, then laying out the back row—burner, receiver, crystal, blue bottle, and scale—along z≈-0.22 to keep everything clear.

I'm repositioning the cone to avoid collisions, then checking spacing against the mortar, candle, and open book—adjusting their x/z coordinates and radii so their footprints don't overlap near the cone's zone.

Now I'm laying out the shelf contents, placing upper and lower shelf items like books, bottles, and jars, and working out the board positions with their thicknesses to anchor each shelf's y-coordinate correctly.

Checking that upper shelf items stay under the height limit (flasks, vials, cones, jars all clear at their scale factors) and that lower shelf books fit within the board clearance. I'm placing the shelf board box with its depth centered at z=-0.24, matching item positions, plus a front gold trim strip and support brackets.

Now I'm sketching out the rug geometry - a flat box with fringe made of small cream boxes looped along each end. I'm estimating total part counts across the whole scene (table, walls, shelves, bottles, books) to make sure I stay under the part budget, roughly tallying bottles at ~6 parts each times 22 bottles, books at ~7 parts each times 15 books, plus everything else.

Setting up color constants...

Defining the flatBook helper function...

I'm adding a paint pattern for the page block so thin horizontal stripes simulate page edges, then working out placement for gold decorative bands across the spine, making sure they're positioned and oriented correctly relative to the spine's face.

Now I'm placing four gold corner accents at the top corners, adding an emblem decal centered on top with the correct up-direction rotation applied via axis-angle math, and setting up the height return value for this piece.

Next I'm defining an upright book shape: spine facing forward, left/right cover panels, a spine panel, an inset pages block in the page color, two decorative bands near top and bottom, and a title plate centered on the spine.

I'll skip leaning/tilt variations for simplicity and plan to write the full scene out in one pass, aiming for around 450 lines covering rods, chains, and a scale reference using small rod segments at the base.

Still defining geometry... lathe profiles for a pillar with a brass body, gold ball finial, and tilted gold beam connecting the posts.

Now I'm working out the beam ends and hanging pan positions, placing chains as thin flat-shaded rods connecting pan rims to the beam tips, and planning the weights inside each pan — brass cylinders on one side, a crystal gem and herb sprig on the other.

I'm deciding the right pan sits higher holding a small glowing gem, while the left pan sits lower weighed down by brass cylinder weights with a ball knob top. Now I'm moving to the mortar and pestle, positioning the pestle as a tapered capsule leaning from inside the bowl up to a resting point outside.

For colors I'm using a mottled teal-marble cel shader for the mortar and pestle, then adding a small herb pile of flattened green spheres in varying shades inside the bowl. I'm deciding to skip the floating sigil rings in favor of a simpler orb-and-ring design, and now moving on to write the stool and card frame flow structure.

Writing potted leaf card frames...

Now I'm adding a sparkle helper that builds thin diamond shapes from octahedron geometries, crossing two at right angles for a glint effect, plus a lantern function, then assembling the full scene with wood trim details.
